ageFourPlusSubset.gpsCoverageNote: Table S3 GPS measurements cover the final 45 days of the grazing period; these do not span the full 84-day derived ADG horizon.

interpretation.use: Separate descriptive reference for pregnant Angus cows in dormant-season grazing, with period body-weight and BCS change and a GPS subset.

adgDerivation.periodEvidence: The article reports body-weight change over the 84-day grazing period (Parsons et al., 2021, Results).
adgDerivation.interpretation: Descriptive average daily weight change derived using the study-level period duration; not a per-animal verified interval, daily time series, or engine prediction.
adgDerivation.durationLimitation: Table S1 has no per-animal start/end dates or observed day counts; 84 days is the period duration reported by the article.

limitations: Cow-season rows repeat some animals across two years and are not 408 independent cows.
167 published IDs occur in both years; keep both year and ID together when making any split or grouped summary.
Table S1 has five missing weight-change values (all in Y1) and three missing BCS-change values; the article does not explain these missing records.
Supplement intake is distinct from total forage DMI.
Table S3 grazing measurements cover only a GPS subset and the last 45 days of grazing.
The cohort is from Montana and is distinct from USDA/CPER and USDA/CGREC.
The source covers ages 1-10 years, including a one-year age class; do not describe every animal as a mature cow.
Derived ADG is period body-weight change divided by the article-reported 84-day grazing period; Table S1 has no per-animal dates or day counts to verify the interval individually.
The dataset lacks matched costs, pasture-stock balance, and a controlled pasture-versus-confinement comparison.
